messages:
alex.li: Heads-up 1: I pushed a new variant for the notification matrix + suppression preview in Figma. The goal: an in-console simulator that shows per-channel payloads, whether an event would actually be sent, and a tiny provenance line explaining why. Figma: https://figma.redwood/notify-matrix-sim-v1 :eyes: maria.g: Love the concept. Can we enumerate the user scenarios the preview should demonstrate? e.g. single-channel alert, multi-channel fanout, per-channel templating, suppressed/within-mute, and fallback-to-secondary channel. alex.li: Yes. Current sims in the frame: 1) Baseline -> primary channel only. 2) Fanout -> slack + email with their respective templates. 3) Suppressed -> shows "Would not send" gray state. 4) Simulated failure -> shows fallback to email. Also severity dropdown so designers can inspect payload differences. jonathan: UX nit: the suppression badge reads "Muted 30m" and that confuses people about scope (global vs per-channel). Proposal: explicit copy "Muted (All channels) 1:30m" for global, and "Muted 1:30m" for channel-level. Or show a small scope label. kyle: Alternative words: "Silenced", "Muted", "Suppressed", "Silence window". "Suppression" feels technical. We should A/B the short phrases with PMs. sophie: A11y: the suppressed card uses low-contrast gray text. Needs AA contrast. Also add non-color indicators (icon + text). Keyboard: when matrix opens focus must land on severity selector; arrow keys to move between channels in the channel list. accessibility-pat: Contrast recs: instead of #9CA3AF on white, use #4B5563 for body text. For suppressed label, use a bolder text token and pair it with an icon. Also add an ARIA-live region so screen readers announce preview changes like "Preview updated: Slack will receive this alert; Email suppressed". maria.g: Good notes. For the preview statuses let's standardize verbs: "Will send", "Suppressed", "Fallbacked". Short verbs are clearer in dense UIs. jonathan: On provenance: preview should show why a decision was made. e.g., a small line like "reason: mute (policy #123)" or "reason: route -> low-priority template". Should we surface rule IDs or only friendly rule names? Debuggers like IDs; PMs prefer readable names. Maybe show both in expanded view. alex.li: I mocked a provenance line under the event header with an info icon. Expanded view shows rule name + ID + link to rule editor. IDs are behind the expansion to reduce noise. Thoughts? sophie: Fine with IDs in expanded. Make sure expansion is keyboard accessible and the copy can be copied to clipboard. No surprise modal behavior. design-bot: alex.li updated frame: notify-matrix-sim-v1 1: preview + simulate-failure added. accessibility-pat: ARIA snippet suggestion for the preview container: 
<div role=\"region\" aria-label=\"Notification preview\" aria-live=\"polite\">
  <!-- preview cards here -->
</div>
Also ensure channel toggles use aria-checked and are in DOM order so screen readers and keyboard users can navigate predictably. kyle: Keyboard flow notes: open modal -> focus severity dropdown -> tab to channel list -> arrow keys left/right or up/down to move channels -> enter to toggle channel on/off -> tab to preview -> esc to close. We should spec this in the interaction doc. maria.g: UX Q: should the preview simulate operational failure modes (rate limit, 5xx) by default? My vote: add an "Advanced" section with a "Simulate failures" checkbox. Default off so PMs won't get confused. jonathan: Simulation toggle is useful for SRE/product handoffs. It helps validate fallback behavior. Also include toggles for "Show provenance" and "Show rule IDs" in advanced options. alex.li: Implemented simulate-failure in Figma as a checkbox with an explanatory tooltip. Also adjusted suppression copy to "Muted (All channels) 1:30m" for global and "Muted 1:30m" for channel-level to reduce ambiguity. sophie: Accessibility extra: color can't be sole indicator. Add icons (check, slash, arrow) and short text. Also use aria-describedby referencing the provenance line when expanded, so screen readers get full context. accessibility-pat: Also recommend that when the preview updates due to keyboard interaction, focus remains logical (don't surprise users by moving focus). Use aria-live for announcement only. For the channel list provide role=\"listbox\" and role=\"option\" semantics if it's a single-select, or checkbox pattern for multi-select. kyle: One more small UI detail: when suppression is global, highlight the global banner at top of matrix with a distinct color and make it sticky while scrolling the channel list. That'll reduce cognitive load. maria.g: I'll run a quick copy preference poll with PMs tomorrow: options include "Muted (All channels)", "Silenced for 30 minutes", "Suppressed: 30m". Will paste the results back here. alex.li: Action items: 1) maria run copy poll, 2) pat run contrast + screen reader pass on the frame, 3) jonathan draft spec for precedence and effective-rule computation for the preview, 4) kyle detail keyboard flows. I'll iterate the Figma frames and post another update later today. Thanks all :sparkles:
